title: Adaptive Fleet-Level Admission & Degraded-Mode Orchestration for Spiky Multi-Region Traffic
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Recent incidents showed short, high-amplitude spikes that saturated specific regions and caused cascading latency violations. Existing lane-based admission logic admits by static priority buckets but lacks a cross-region viewpoint or graceful fidelity proposals that can be enacted without full request failures. Goal: Implement a fleet-level admission controller that coordinates priority queues, token reservoirs, and per-tenant degradation policies across regions to keep SLOs stable during spikes while preserving best-effort throughput and minimizing hard rejects. The feature will: 1) introduce a cross-region admission feed to rebalance soft-credits across regions during failovers; 2) provide a deferred-execution reservoir for low-priority work (best-effort queues with TTL); 3) expose per-tenant graceful-degradation profiles (compress responses, trim completions, downgrade model variant) that can be applied automatically when global or region-local SLOs degrade. Non-goals: this ticket does not implement new quantization or kernel-level performance work, and it will not change billing logic. It also avoids replacing current canary rollout mechanisms; the rollout will be gradual behind flags.
acceptance_criteria: Fleet admission can shift up to 25% of soft-credit tokens from a failing region to warm regions within 60s of a failover trigger
Low-priority deferred-reservoir holds up to 10k requests with configurable TTL and exposes metrics for drained/skipped counts
Graceful-degradation profiles can be attached to tenants and include at least three actions: compress-response, model-variant-fallback, and token-trim; policies are selectable by percent and order
No SLO regression (>10% increase in p95 latency) for high-priority tenants during a synthetic multi-region spike test (workload harness attached)
Feature gated behind runtime flag with operator override and observability dashboards showing credits, reservoir depth, and applied degradations
tasks: Design: define soft-credit accounting and reconciliation protocol for cross-region transfers
Implementation: reservoir queue with TTL and eviction hooks
Implementation: admission controller plugin to consult tenant degradation profiles and apply actions atomically
Observability: dashboards, alerts, and tracing hooks for admission decisions
E2E tests: chaos and synthetic spike harness spanning 3 regions
Docs: runtime operator runbook and API docs for profiling/degradation config
Rollout: gradual canary behind feature flag in staging then prod
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (staging): enable flag for internal traffic only; run synthetic spike harness across 3 regions
Stage 2 (canary): enable for 5% of tenant traffic by routing token subset; monitor p50/p95 and error budgets
Stage 3 (ramp): 25% traffic after 48h of stable metrics; provide opt-out per tenant
Stage 4 (global): full rollout with automated fallback to previous admission logic on circuit-breaker trips
testing_plan: Unit tests for token-transfer reconciliation and edge cases (network partitions)
Integration tests exercising reservoir eviction, TTL expiry, and deferred-execution callbacks
Chaos test: region partition where primary region loses 40% capacity while warm regions accept transferred soft credits
SLO regression test harness reproducing prior incident shape and asserting high-priority tenant latency preservation
Load test: long-tail distribution of requests to validate reservoir drains without pressure on hot-path kernels
observability_and_metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency by tenant and by applied-degradation
design_notes: Use a CRDT-like reconciliation for soft-credit balances to ensure eventual consistency across controller replicas rather than synchronous locks
Prefer eventual transfer with backpressure signals; immediate hard moves create oscillation under flapping conditions
Graceful-degradation actions are ordered and idempotent: compress-response -> token-trim -> model-variant-fallback
Default tenant profile is conservative (only token-trim) — admins can opt into aggressive degradations for cost-sensitive workloads
Avoid storing large request bodies in reservoir; persist only pointers and minimal metadata to rehydrate if execution proceeds
tradeoffs_and_risks: Risk: Cross-region token movement increases coupling between regions; we accept eventual consistency to avoid head-of-line locks
Tradeoff: Deferred-reservoir reduces hard rejects but increases tail latency for low-priority work; must be telemetry-driven
Risk: Incorrectly scoped degradation profiles could silently reduce quality for important customers — require explicit opt-in for aggressive modes
Tradeoff: More complex admission logic increases cognitive load for operators — we mitigate with clear dashboards and an operator-facing panic button
